Hamper

/HAM-per/ - rhymes with camper · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Hamper means to slow something down and make it more difficult.

Loose gravel hampered the cyclists on the final climb, forcing even the leaders to dismount and push.

Worked Example

Oversized mittens hampered every step of the scouts' knot-tying badge — twine slipped, loops collapsed — until the leader let them work bare-handed for the test.

Hamper never stops a thing outright; that's what makes it different from 'halt' or 'block.' The effort continues, just slower, clumsier, and more costly — like walking with your laces tied together.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hobble: to cripple movement almost completely

slow: the plain word — less about tangling and difficulty

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ease: to make something smoother and less difficult

speed: to hurry a thing along

Where it sits · how badly progress is slowed — inconvenience → hamper → hobble

inconvenience vs. hamper: An inconvenience is milder than hampering — it annoys and costs a little time, but the work rolls on much as before.

hobble vs. hamper: Hobbling goes even further than hampering — the effort is left limping, barely able to move at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hamper

Root — hamper: to entangle, to impede (Middle English hamperen, origin uncertain)

Put it together

Put it together: There is nothing to peel off here: hamper reached English whole, as Middle English hamperen, 'to entangle,' and scholars have never settled where it came from before that. The picture inside it has stayed constant for six centuries — something snagged and dragging, still moving but paying for every step.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: The verb hamper has no traceable root and no English relatives. Even the picnic hamper is a stranger: that basket comes from hanaper, an Old French word for a case that held drinking cups — the two words merely collided in spelling.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral

Hamper is the all-purpose word for friction — fog hampers a search, paperwork hampers a launch, an injury hampers a season. Use 'block' or 'halt' when progress actually stops; hamper means it continues at a price. Its close cousin hinder, which also appears in this unit, is nearly interchangeable, though hamper leans a little harder on the image of being tangled or weighed down.
